title: Robert Hoffman as a young bicycle racer
summary: Before music, he and a friend ran New Orleans's first bicycle shop and raced at sixteen.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: I was wondering about the baseball games. Did they have music at them ever?
I know sometimes in Heinemann Park when they'd have a big game, they'd have a band.
A band, maybe. But I don't think he was ever involved in any music. And you know what Bob was when he was a young man? Believe it or not. He was a bicycle racer.

He and another young fellow. He used to show me the house that was sitting on St. Charles Avenue. A beautiful residence. It's a residence that's still up there. That had a basement to it. It was built up high. High steps, you know, went up. And he said that this other boy, and I don't even know who it was, and he, when they were 16 years old, they had the first bicycle shop in New Orleans where they sold and repaired bicycles. And the path, they used to have the races. And they ran from some point down in town out of Shell Road. And it came out at City Park Avenue right by the bayou there. And I think that's the ground they covered, you know, in the races. I imagine they had them on Sunday afternoon. I'm not quite sure about that. Because I only heard him talk about that. That was when he was young, you know.
